name: Bell Labs 96-element CCD line imager
description: Bell Labs researchers fabricated a 96-element silicon CCD that integrated light as charge packets and shifted them to produce an analog video signal. Mechanical movement supplied the second scan axis for reproducing printed text and a grayscale photograph.

events.statement: Popular Electronics described Bell Labs’ operating 96-element CCD scanner and the use of mechanical motion to scan documents.

evidence.supports: The contemporary account describes operation of the prototype, its 96 sensing elements and the optical scan setup.

date.basis: Issue date of IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices 18(11).

events.statement: Tompsett and colleagues published results from a 96-element CCD that reproduced printed type and a grayscale image by line scanning.
events.caveats: The tests used a linear sensor and mechanical scanning. The paper sketches an area imager as a possible further design.

evidence.supports: The authors report operating an imager, with reproduced images and details of the line scan.
Independent RCA account describes the 96-element Bell array and its scan method.

earliest_record.rationale: The July account documents the 96-element scanner before the researchers’ detailed November paper.

links.statement: The line imager implemented Boyle and Smith’s charge-coupled readout, collecting photo-generated carriers and clocking them along a single row to an output diode.
links.caveats: The reported apparatus admitted light through gaps between front electrodes. The original concept paper proposed illumination from the substrate side.

evidence.supports: Proposes integrating photo-generated charge in potential wells and shifting it out through a register.
The experiment implements clocked transfer to read out an optical scan.
An independent RCA engineer explicitly attributes the original three-phase structure to Boyle and Smith and describes the Bell group’s operating line imager.
